docs.title: About Unimined
docs.text: Welcome to Unimined, a unified Minecraft modding environment that supports both modern and legacy environments. Whether you're working with the latest Minecraft versions or exploring older builds, Unimined provides a comprehensive set of tools to help you build mods with ease.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Unified Modding Environment: Supports various Minecraft mod loaders and offers tools for a seamless experience across different modding platforms.
  • Custom Loader Support: Create and integrate your own loaders with the flexibility of Unimined.

docs.title: Supported Loaders
docs.text:
• Fabric
  • Quilt
  • Forge
  • Neoforge
  • just plain jarmodding
    • Modloader
    • JarModAgent
  • ~~Flint Loader~~ (removed — maven.flintloader.net offline)
  • Rift
  • Craftbukkit/Spigot
  • Paper
  • Liteloader

docs.title: Planned
docs.text:
• Better Bukkit-derivitive support
    • Spigot currently just kinda runs buildtools in the backround.
  • Sponge
  • NilLoader

docs.title: Custom Loaders
docs.text: you can create a custom patching/transforming process for minecraft, for example PrcraftExampleMod's buildsrc dir.

docs.title: Planned Features

  • Datagen

docs.title: Migrating from 1.x to 2.0
docs.text: Unimined 2.0 splits the monolithic unimined { } extension into per-domain plugins with their own extensions. Groovy scripts that call removed 1.x verbs now get a migration note naming the new form; Kotlin DSL scripts fail at compile time — this table maps old calls to their 2.0 equivalents.

docs.title: Environment configuration
docs.text:
1.x 2.0 unimined.minecraft(sourceSet) { } unimined.minecraft { } + per-source-set env (minecraft { sourceSet("main") { } }) unimined.reIndev(sourceSet) { } env-level infra config inside unimined.minecraft { } unimined.bta(sourceSet) { } same — env-level inside unimined.minecraft { }

Loader declaration moves onto the environment: loader("fabric", "0.16.0") / loader("fg1", "0.1.5") / env.jarmod("x") / env.fg1("x") / env.customSearge().

docs.title: Remap pipeline
docs.text: 1.x 2.0 remap hooks inside unimined { } unimined.remap { } — step verbs (unpick(...), applyClassTweaker {}, sourceRemap {}) per surface, both Groovy and Kotlin. Source remapping runs through UML's source remapper by default; jst {} remains as an explicit engine opt-in (verification/alternate engine), not a peer default unimined.migrateMappings(sourceSet) { } unimined.migrateMappings("main") { } (env id), or unimined.migrate { }

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text: The ~20 unimined.*Maven()/unimined.*Repos() helpers (fabricMaven, minecraftForgeMaven, curseMaven, jitpack, spigot, quiltMaven, ornitheMaven, legacyFabricMaven, neoForgedMaven, cleanroomRepos, modrinthMaven, …) are gone: loader repositories are auto-registered per environment in 2.0. Remove the calls; use a normal repositories {} block for anything custom. modsRemapRepo is likewise managed internally.

docs.title: Other moves
docs.text:
1.x 2.0 mod/transform config inside unimined { } unimined.mod { }, unimined.transform { } global toolchain toggle unimined.useToolchains = false env java override unimined.javaVersion (delegates to the main env) jvmArgs += "-javaagent:/path/agent.jar" javaagents.add(file("agent.jar")) on the run config — a typed file collection resolved to -javaagent: flags at launch

Unknown or removed verbs raise a GradleException naming the replacement — read the message; it points here.

docs.title: Declared-source provider (legacydist)
docs.text:
New in 2.0: environments whose game jar has no manifest-backed provider declare the artifact directly instead of shipping a bespoke provider — BTA/ReIndev-style jars, pre-1.8 bukkit, offline/air-gapped artifacts:

unimined.minecraft.main.legacydist {
    file("libs/bta-7.3-client.jar")      // or maven("g:a:v"),
    // url("https://...", sha256 = "..."), producer("tool", "...")
    namespace = "official"               // jar's production namespace
    format = "obf"                       // optional — raw->dev remap view
}

legacydist {} selects provider("legacydist") implicitly; the jar is cached by content hash and reported with the declared namespace/format. URLs are pinned by SHA-256 (warned-but-allowed when omitted); maven coordinates resolve at declaration time.

docs.title: Adapters
docs.text:
Adapters are opt-in Gradle plugins that bridge third-party tools into Unimined. They live in unimined-adapters/ and publish as xyz.wagyourtail.unimined:unimined-adapter-<tool>.

They share a common shape:

  • Opt-in — applying an adapter without its target tool is a no-op (or a logged warning); they activate via withPlugin when the tool's plugin is present.
  • Stable plugin ids — adapter coordinates may move between artifacts, but plugins {} ids do not change.
  • Environment-scoped — most adapters hang their DSL off each sourceSet("...")/environment block.
Adapter Plugin id Bridges Java JvmDowngrader xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.jvmdg JvmDowngrader bytecode downgrade 17+ ModPublisher xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.publish-modpublisher ModPublisher uploads 17+ PatchBase xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-patchbase PatchBase patch sets 17+ Forgix xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-forgix Forgix loader-jar merge 17+ Stonecutter xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-stonecutter Stonecutter version envs 21+ ExpectPlatform xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-expectplatform ExpectPlatform agent 17+ 
plugins {
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined")
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-patchbase") version "2.0.0"
}

docs.title: ExpectPlatform adapter
docs.text:
Plugin id: xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-expectplatform

Bridges ExpectPlatform into Unimined. ExpectPlatform's own insertAgent(JavaExecSpec) can't attach to Unimined runs (they aren't JavaExecSpecs), and dev-vs-prod needs different handling — the adapter covers both:

  • Dev runs get the javaagent + -Dexpect.* sysprops, including -Dexpect.side so the agent strips the other side's @Environment-annotated members at classload (dev classes are raw; loaders scan bytes before transforms — issue #4)
  • The prod jar gets ExpectPlatform's transform applied statically as a JAR-surface step — @ExpectPlatform redirects, @PlatformOnly filtering, and annotation remaps are resolved into the artifact, so runProd* runs and shipped jars need no agent
  • modImplementation/modRuntimeOnly are marked for ExpectPlatform's artifact transform, so resolved mod jars (e.g. a shared common module) arrive already platform-transformed

Requires both xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.expect-platform and xyz.wagyourtail.unimined applied — the adapter activates when both are present.

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text:
The canonical multi-loader setup — the @ExpectPlatform stub lives in the shared env, one <pkg>/<platform>/<Class>Impl class per loader env:

my-mod/
├── build.gradle.kts
└── src/
    ├── main/java/com/example/
    │   └── Platform.java              # @ExpectPlatform stubs
    ├── fabric/java/com/example/fabric/
    │   └── PlatformImpl.java          # real impl for "fabric"
    └── forge/java/com/example/forge/
        └── PlatformImpl.java          # real impl for "forge"

docs.title: build.gradle.kts
docs.text:
plugins {
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined") version "..."
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.expect-platform") version "1.2.0"
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-expectplatform") version "..."
}

unimined {
    minecraft {
        version = "1.20.1"
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")
        expectPlatform {
            platform("fabric") // the @ExpectPlatform platform name
        }

        sourceSet("forge") {
            version = "1.20.1"
            loader("forge", "47.2.0")
            expectPlatform { platform("forge") }
        }
    }
}

dependencies {
    "mainImplementation"(expectPlatform.annotationsDep)
}

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
// src/main/java/com/example/Platform.java — shared env
public final class Platform {

    // Body is replaced at transform time by
    // com/example/<platform>/PlatformImpl.loaderName()
    @ExpectPlatform
    public static String loaderName() {
        throw new AssertionError();
    }

    // Present only on the listed platforms — filtered out elsewhere
    @PlatformOnly("forge")
    public static void forgeOnlyThing() {}
}

// src/fabric/java/com/example/fabric/PlatformImpl.java
public final class PlatformImpl {
    public static String loaderName() { return "fabric"; }
}

// src/forge/java/com/example/forge/PlatformImpl.java
public final class PlatformImpl {
    public static String loaderName() { return "forge"; }
}

@Environment(EnvType.CLIENT) marks side-only members with ExpectPlatform's own annotation — in the prod jar it is remapped to the loader's side annotation (see the table below), and in dev the agent strips the other side's members at classload.

docs.title: Per-env knobs
docs.text:
platform(name, remap) sets platformName/remap on the env's expectPlatform extension and marks its mod-dep configurations. All of it resolves lazily — a common env's platform(...) propagates to combineWith children by convention, and each knob is per-env overridable:

Property Default Purpose enabled true master switch — off: no agent, no jar step agent true off: drop the javaagent + sysprops from runs, keep the static jar transform platformName inherited the ExpectPlatform platform name remap table + inherited + explicit annotation-descriptor remaps (see below) stripAnnotations false strip ExpectPlatform's own annotations from output

docs.title: The @Environment remap table is filled for you
docs.text:
remap defaults to a built-in table for the env's platform — the same maps ExpectPlatform's README documents:

  • fabric (and legacyfabric/babric/ornithe) → net.fabricmc.api.Environment/EnvType
  • quilt → org.quiltmc.loader.api.minecraft.MinecraftOnlyIn/EnvType
  • forge → era-picked by env.version: ≥1.13 net.minecraftforge.api.distmarker.OnlyIn/Dist, 1.8–1.12 net.minecraftforge.fml.relauncher.SideOnly/Side, ≤1.7.10 cpw.mods.fml.relauncher.SideOnly/Side
  • neoforge → net.neoforged.api.distmarker.OnlyIn/Dist
  • cleanroom → the 1.12-era fml table

Explicit remap entries merge over the table (table < inherited env < explicit). Loaders with no side-annotation convention (vanilla, jarmod, modloader, bukkit family) get none.

docs.title: Manual jar step
docs.text:
The same static transform is declared as a JAR-surface verb when you want it on a specific product instead of env-wide:

jar {
    expectPlatform { platformName.set("fabric") }
}

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Java 17+
  • xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.expect-platform ≥ 1.2.0 for side stripping; the agent jar resolves from the applied plugin's version

docs.title: Forgix (loader-jar merge)
docs.text: Adapter plugin xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-forgix (unimined-adapter-forgix) merges per-loader production jars with Forgix's engine (Forgix.mergeLoaders) and publishes the result on the consumable mergedElements configuration (classifier merged).

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text:
my-mod/
├── build.gradle.kts
└── src/
    ├── main/         # common env
    ├── fabric/       # fabric env → remapFabricJar
    └── forge/        # forge env → remapForgeJar

docs.title: build.gradle.kts
docs.text:
plugins {
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined") version "..."
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-forgix") version "..."
}

unimined {
    minecraft {
        version = "1.20.1"
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")

        sourceSet("forge") {
            version = "1.20.1"
            loader("forge", "47.2.0")
        }
    }
}

That's the whole configuration — mergeLoaderJars discovers every bound non-auxiliary environment's production jar automatically. A typical multi-loader project writes zero merge config.

Forgix's own Gradle plugin is not required — its merge(name) DSL and mergeJars task only support multi-project layouts (merge names must be subproject names, and its jar-resolution heuristic checks the project before inputJar), so flat env-per-source-set projects can't use it. The adapter drives the layout-agnostic engine directly from mergeLoaderJars instead.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Three sources feed the merge, in increasing precedence:

  1. Bound environments — auto-injected. Every non-auxiliary env's production jar (remap<Env>Jar, or the env's plain jar), keyed by loaderSpec.name (env id as fallback; same-loader collisions become <name>-<envId>). Needs no configuration.
  2. forgix { } DSL — optional. When io.github.pacifistmc.forgix is also applied, entries in forgix.mergeConfigurations feed in (explicit inputJar wins; the subproject heuristic is the fallback). On flat projects, write them via the map — upstream's merge(name) validates before running its action and always throws for non-subproject names.
  3. loaderMerge.from(...) — optional override. Only needed for extra inputs or key collisions — the env feed already covers the standard case:
uniminedLoaderMerge {
    from(
        "quilt" to tasks.named("remapQuiltJar").flatMap { it.archiveFile },
    )
}

Inputs may be Files, task references, or providers — task-output providers carry their producer, so inputs always build before the merge runs.

docs.title: Consumers
docs.text: adapter-modpublisher prefers the mergedElements artifact as the upload artifact automatically — and suppresses the per-loader jars — so applying all three plugins means a merged multi-loader jar is what gets published.

docs.title: JvmDowngrader adapter
docs.text:
Plugin id: xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.jvmdg

Bridges JvmDowngrader into Unimined so environments targeting ancient JVMs (Java 8 and below-era loaders) can compile on a modern JDK while producing downgraded bytecode for dev runs, jars, and api jars.

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text:
my-mod/
├── build.gradle.kts
└── src/main/

docs.title: build.gradle.kts
docs.text:
plugins {
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined") version "..."
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.jvmdg") version "..."
}

unimined {
    minecraft {
        version = "1.7.10"
        loader("forge", "10.13.4.1614")
        // downgrading is already on — only write jvmdowngrader {}
        // to change the inferred target or opt this env out
        jvmdowngrader(8)
        // or jvmdowngrader { enabled.set(false) }
    }
}

Downgrading is on by default for every environment — applying the plugin is the opt-in. target conventions to each env's own Java floor (the version-json javaVersion, floored at 7 for ≤1.6.4-era), so most projects need no per-env config at all.

Envs whose compile output is already at/below the target pass through untouched. When enabled it:

  • supplies a downgrade step on the JAR surface — the shipped jar carries downgraded bytecode
  • produces a downgraded api jar for downstream consumers
  • makes dev run* tasks launch against downgraded copies of your compile outputs — old forge runtimes (ASM 4 / patched ASM 5.2) can't read modern class files, so this is required for them to run at all

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Java 17+ to run the build (the adapter itself targets 17)
  • Consumes xyz.wagyourtail.jvmdowngrader:jvmdowngrader-java-api:2.0.1 directly — do not also apply JvmDowngrader's own Gradle plugin,
  • Old-forge dev runs require this when your compile target is newer than Java 8

docs.title: ModPublisher adapter
docs.text:
Plugin id: xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.publish-modpublisher

Feeds your build's production artifacts + metadata into ModPublisher's own publisher { } DSL as conventions — the adapter owns selection and plumbing only; ModPublisher's engine is applied by you. There is no adapter DSL: publisher { } stays the single surface for what can't be inferred, and anything you set there always wins.

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text:
my-mod/
├── build.gradle.kts
└── src/
    ├── main/         # common env → common prod jar
    ├── fabric/       # fabric env → remapFabricJar
    └── forge/        # forge env → remapForgeJar

docs.title: build.gradle.kts
docs.text:
plugins {
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined") version "..."
    id("com.hypherionmc.modutils.modpublisher") version "2.2.4"
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.publish-modpublisher") version "..."
}

unimined {
    minecraft {
        version = "1.20.1"
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")

        sourceSet("forge") {
            version = "1.20.1"
            loader("forge", "47.2.0")
        }
    }
}

// artifacts + loaders + gameVersions + version already conventioned —
// write publisher{} only for creds, platform ids, and release metadata
publisher {
    apiKeys {
        curseforge(providers.environmentVariable("CURSE_TOKEN").get())
        modrinth(providers.environmentVariable("MODRINTH_TOKEN").get())
    }
    curseID.set("1234")
    modrinthID.set("abc")
    versionType.set("release")
}

docs.title: What conventions in
docs.text:
publisher field Convention artifact the forgix mergedElements jar when adapter-forgix is applied, else the first bound env's production jar (remap<Env>Jar when it remaps, else jar) additionalFiles the remaining per-loader prod jars loaders bound envs' loaderSpec.names gameVersions bound envs' versions version project.version

Selection: the merged artifact wins when present and suppresses the per-loader jars; aux envs (gametest/datagen) are excluded; dev jars are never selectable.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Java 17+
  • ModPublisher applied separately — the adapter is plumbing, not a redistribution
  • API keys live in publisher.apiKeys { } as ModPublisher expects — resolve them from env vars/gradle properties; they are never logged by the adapter

docs.title: PatchBase adapter
docs.text:
Plugin id: xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-patchbase

Bridges PatchBase patch sets into Unimined environments. Two flows:

  • Authoring a patch set against Minecraft (a "patchbase modloader" project — the git repo carries only patch files)
  • Consuming patch sets — modding against an MC jar mutated by .binpatch/.bdiff entries, the same seam Forge binpatches occupy

The adapter consumes the standalone patchbase artifact (xyz.wagyourtail.unimined:patchbase:2.0.0) — PatchBase's core has no Unimined dependency; this plugin is only the env bridge.

docs.title: Project layout (authoring)
docs.text:
my-patchbase/
├── build.gradle.kts
├── patches/            # git-tracked unified diffs — the repo's
│                       #   only real content
└── src/main/java/      # generated patched sources — gitignore this

docs.title: build.gradle.kts (authoring)
docs.text:
plugins {
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined") version "..."
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-patchbase") version "..."
}

unimined {
    minecraft {
        version = "1.7.10"
        patchBaseCreator()
    }
}

docs.title: Consuming patch sets
docs.text:
unimined {
    minecraft {
        version = "1.7.10"
        patchBase("com.example:my-patches:1.0")
    }
}

Resolves the dep onto the env's patchBaseMain configuration and applies its class patches to the environment's MC jar before remapping — compile classpath and dev runs both see the patched game. Patch entries are .binpatch (standard record) or .bdiff (PatchBase's checksum+gdiff unit); all other jar entries copy over verbatim.

docs.title: Authoring a patch set
docs.text:
sourceSet("main") {
    patchBaseCreator()
}

Wires three tasks per environment:

Task Does applySourcePatch<Env> applies patches/ unified diffs onto the gen<Env>Sources output, writing only patch-covered files to src/<env>/java (generated — gitignore it) so compile + JarModAgent see patched sources createSourcePatch<Env> diffs src/<env>/java back into patches/ — keeps the git-tracked patch source in sync createClassPatch<Env> diffs the remap<Env>Jar output vs minecraftRaw into the shippable patch jar (classifier patch[-env])

Only patches/ belongs in git. The generated patched sources and the built patch jar are artifacts.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Patch sets bind to a base jar. .binpatch/.bdiff entries carry a checksum of the class they were built against — create patch jars against the env's pre-remap base (minecraftRaw), which is what createClassPatch uses, or consumers' checksums won't match
  • The dev flow mirrors Forge binpatches: the patch jar mutates the MC jar, so the loader's classes exist for compile and runtime without loader sources or a recompile

docs.title: Stonecutter adapter
docs.text:
Plugin id: xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-stonecutter

Bridges Stonecutter into Unimined for multi-version projects. When dev.kikugie.stonecutter is applied, every Unimined environment's version conventions to the chiseled project's version (stonecutter.current.version) — so the shared build script doesn't repeat version = stonecutter.current.version in every target. An explicit version on an environment always wins.

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text:
my-mod/
├── settings.gradle.kts      # stonecutter plugin + version tree
├── build.gradle.kts         # central script — applied to every
│                            #   chiseled version project
├── gradle.properties
├── src/main/                # shared sources (java/kotlin/resources)
└── versions/
    ├── 1.20.4/
    │   └── gradle.properties  # per-version dep versions
    └── 1.21.1/
        └── gradle.properties

docs.title: settings.gradle.kts
docs.text:
plugins {
    id("dev.kikugie.stonecutter") version "0.9.8"
}

stonecutter {
    shared {
        versions("1.20.4", "1.21.1")
        vcsVersion.set("1.21.1")
    }
    kotlinController.set(true)
}

docs.title: build.gradle.kts (central script)
docs.text:
Applied to every version project — the adapter supplies env.version from the chiseled version, so this script stays version-free:

plugins {
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined") version "..."
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-stonecutter") version "..."
    kotlin("jvm") version "..."
}

group = "com.example.mymod"

unimined {
    minecraft {
        // env.version conventions to stonecutter.current.version —
        // "1.20.4" when building that project, "1.21.1" for the other
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")
    }
}

dependencies {
    // per-version dep versions come from each version's
    // gradle.properties — stonecutter exposes them as `deps.*`
    // project properties
    modImplementation("net.fabricmc:fabric-loader:${property("deps.fabric_loader")}")
    modImplementation("net.fabricmc.fabric-api:fabric-api:${property("deps.fabric_api")}")
}

docs.title: versions/1.20.4/gradle.properties
docs.text:
deps.fabric_loader=0.16.9
deps.fabric_api=0.102.0+1.20.4

Per-version build-script overrides are also possible (versions/<ver>/build.gradle.kts); the shared script still wins only where it doesn't set explicit values.

docs.title: Multi-loader envs
docs.text:
Stonecutter wires sourceSets.all { }, so Unimined's env-per- source-set model works per version project — each env's sources get the same shared + version-specific layering and chisel comment processing as main:

my-mod/
└── src/
    ├── main/                # shared across loaders and versions
    ├── fabric/              # fabric env sources
    └── forge/               # forge env sources
versions/1.20.4/
└── src/
    ├── main/                # version-specific overrides
    └── forge/               # per-version, per-loader overrides

// central build.gradle.kts
unimined {
    minecraft {
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")            // main env

        sourceSet("forge") {
            loader("forge", "47.2.0")         // forge env — also
        }                                     //   chiseled per version
    }
}

Each version project then produces jar + remapFabricJar + remapForgeJar for its own version — the full version×loader matrix inside one chiseled project. Ordering is safe: sourceSets.all is a live callback, so envs created after Stonecutter's plugin is applied are still picked up. This composes with adapter-expectplatform, adapter-forgix (merges that version's loader jars), and adapter-modpublisher.

Upstream Stonecutter templates sometimes encode the loader in the version id instead (versions("1.20.4-fabric")) — that also works but gives one project per loader×version pair; the per-source-set layout above keeps all loaders for a version in one project.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Java 21 — Stonecutter publishes Java-21 bytecode, so the adapter module targets 21 too (the rest of Unimined stays at 17)
  • dev.kikugie.stonecutter must be applied; without it the adapter logs a warning and does nothing

docs.title: unimined-cli
docs.text:
unimined generates complete modding environments — the single entry point for new projects. Binaries ship per-platform (native .kexe, fat jar, Node build).

unimined new mymod --group com.example --version 1.20.1 --loader fabric=0.16.0
unimined init                       # in an existing directory

Highlights:

  • multiloader — repeat --loader; add --modules for the common+per-loader subproject layout
  • products — --product bta|reindev|nsss|custom:<name>
  • eras — --jarmod, --jars split|merged, --side client|server|merged, era-aware forge entrypoints
  • escape hatches — --mappings "<dsl>", --extra "<line>", --var key=val, --no-wrapper, --include-build, --toolchain

Full flag list: CLI Reference.

docs.title: First Project
docs.text:
A flat, single-loader mod environment on native Minecraft:

Key pieces:

  • unimined { minecraft { } } — an environment bound to the main source set. version is the MC version; loader("fabric", "…") applies a loader.
  • mappings { } — the remap chain (yarn(10) here; see Mappings).
  • mod { } — mod metadata (id, name, version, depends) emitted into the loader's descriptor at build time.
  • dependencies { } — env mod* configurations take mod artifacts and remap them onto your mappings.

Next: more environments, other products, or a multi-module layout.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Unimined 2.0 is a Gradle plugin. In settings.gradle.kts, register the maven repo and (for local composite development) optionally the includeBuild path:

Then apply the plugin in build.gradle.kts:

plugins {
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined") version "2.0.0-SNAPSHOT"
}

Skip the typing

unimined-cli new mymod --group com.example --version 1.20.1 --loader fabric=0.16.0 emits this whole structure for you — see unimined-cli.

docs.title: Auth
docs.text:
Run configurations carry a typed auth { } spec — each run decides how its session is produced. 2.0 has no project-global runs.auth: per-run, provider-backed, and nothing token-shaped ever lands on the configuration model or in the config cache.

unimined {
    runs {
        named("client") {
            auth { microsoft() }
        }
        named("server") {
            auth { offline("DevServer") }
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Verbs
docs.text:
Verb Session produced offline(name) Offline-mode session — deterministic UUID from the player name (default) microsoft() Microsoft account — stored credential + silent refresh custom(provider) Any AuthProvider — the extension point for third-party auth (Ely.by, launchers) injected(prefix) Session read from UNIMINED_AUTH_* env vars at execution — the CI path

username = "x" on a run is the back-compat shorthand for auth { offline("x") } — an explicit auth spec wins over it.

docs.title: A default for every run
docs.text:
runs { auth { } } configures the default applied to all runs — per-run auth/username values always win:

unimined {
    runs {
        auth { microsoft() }         // everything logs in...
        named("server") {
            auth { offline("Srv") }  // ...except the server
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Microsoft login
docs.text:
Run loginMicrosoft once on a machine with a browser — it prints the device-code URL + code, completes the MSA → Xbox → Minecraft chain, and stores the credential. Runs then consume the store with a silent refresh; they never prompt mid-launch — a missing credential fails fast with the remediation in the message.

Store: <unimined global cache>/auth/credentials.json, written 0600, one serialized session per username.

docs.title: Gradle properties
docs.text: Property Default Purpose unimined.auth.username — Account selector for loginMicrosoft and for microsoft() runs when more than one user is stored unimined.auth.encrypt false Opt-in AES-256-encrypted store, key from the OS keyring via java-keyring (loaded reflectively — add com.github.javakeyring:java-keyring to the build classpath). No plaintext fallback: encrypt on + no keyring = explicit failure unimined.auth.storeCredentials true false reads+refreshes stored credentials in memory only — nothing is written back

docs.title: CI / headless
docs.text:
runs.named("client") { auth { injected() } }

reads UNIMINED_AUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN (required) plus optional UNIMINED_AUTH_USERNAME/_UUID/_XUID/_USER_TYPE at execution — provision them from the runner's secret store. Alternatively run :loginMicrosoft locally and ship the resulting credentials.json (which still resolves through the same unimined.auth.* props).

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Sessions materialize inside the run task's execution — access tokens never appear in task inputs, the config cache, or logs.
  • auth { injected() } never writes to the credential store.
  • Old single-player-era launchers passed session details as user_properties — the resolver still substitutes it; Microsoft sessions leave it empty.

docs.title: Datagen
docs.text:
env.datagen() declares an auxiliary environment for data generation — separate sources, its own classpath, but sharing the parent env's Minecraft/loader/mappings via implicit-parent inheritance:

unimined {
    minecraft {
        version = "1.20.1"
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")

        datagen()                          // env "data" → runData
        // or: datagen(client = true)      // client-side pack
    }
}

docs.title: What it wires
docs.text:
• src/data/ (or src/<env>Data/) — your datagen entrypoints live here, compiled against the parent's classpath
  • src/<parent>/generated is added to the parent env's resources — generated JSON/tags/recipes land in the mod jar automatically
  • A run<Data> configuration materializes from the loader's datagenMain/datagenArgs capabilities — {output} in the arg template resolves to src/<env>/generated
  • client = true appends the loader's datagenClientArg (fabric: --client) for client-side packs

The mod still declares its loader's datagen entrypoint itself (e.g. fabric's fabric-datagen key in fabric.mod.json) — unimined only provides the env, classpath, and run.

docs.title: Naming
docs.text: datagen() defaults to data on main, <env>Data elsewhere; datagen("mygen") overrides. It's an aux env (isAuxEnv) — excluded from publication and loader-jar merging.

docs.title: Loaders without datagen
docs.text: If the loader descriptor has no datagenMain capability, the run still registers but launches the plain game — a warning is logged. Forge supplies datagenArgs through its userdev capabilities; older loaders need a manual runs.named("data") { mainClass = … }.

docs.title: Mod dependencies (artifacts)
docs.text:
Each env exposes mod* configurations scoped to its source set — mod jars land remapped onto your mappings:

dependencies {
    modImplementation("maven:coord")
    modCompileOnly("maven:coord")
    modLocalRuntime("maven:coord")
}

docs.title: Loader apis
docs.text: unimined.loaderApi(name, version) resolves a loader's api artifact bundle; loaderApiModule(name, module, version) resolves one sub-module. Both also record the api modid into mod { depends }.

docs.title: Metadata-only dependencies
docs.text: mod { depend("modid", "versionRange") } declares runtime deps in the emitted mod metadata without touching the classpath.

docs.title: Environments
docs.text:
An environment is a Minecraft instance bound to a source set — the unit that owns a product, loaders, mappings, run configs, and mod* dependency configurations.

unimined {
    minecraft {
        // bound to main by default
        version = "1.20.1"
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")
        // or a named source-set env:
        sourceSet("server") {
            loader("forge", "47.2.0")
            side = Side.SERVER
        }
    }
}
  • sourceSet(name) binds the env to a source set (default main); sibling envs are independent — combineWith("other") (optionally with EnvironmentSections) composes one into another, and nested envs (datagen()/gametest()) inherit their parent implicitly.
  • side selects Side.CLIENT/SERVER/MERGED (example).
  • Multiple envs in one project = flat multi-env; multi-module is the alternative.

Envs are also the scope of mod { } metadata and runs { }.

docs.title: Gametests
docs.text:
env.gametest() declares an auxiliary environment for in-game JUnit tests — real game launches orchestrated per test, not a plain JVM test run:

unimined {
    minecraft {
        version = "1.20.1"
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")

        gametest()                         // env "gametest"
    }
}

docs.title: What it wires
docs.text:
• src/gametest/ (or src/<env>Gametest/) — test sources on the parent's classpath via implicit-parent inheritance
  • The loader's gametestJunit coordinate is added to testImplementation ({loader} in the template resolves to the env's loader version — e.g. fabric-loader-junit) and the env's test task is switched to useJUnitPlatform()
  • Client gametests: the gametest env's own <env>GametestClient run gets the loader's gametestClientJvmArgs (-D... flags) — {modid} resolves against mod { id }. Entrypoint classes are declared by the loader (fabric-gametest / fabric-client-gametest keys in fabric.mod.json)
  • Server gametests run inside the JUnit orchestration — no separate run needed

The mod still registers its loader-specific gametest entrypoints — unimined provides the env, classpath, JUnit artifact, and the armed client run.

docs.title: Loaders without gametest support
docs.text:
If the descriptor has no gametestJunit capability the env still compiles (a warning notes the missing artifact) — write your own gametestImplementation coordinate or orchestrate launches via a custom runs.create(...).

Aux env (isAuxEnv) — excluded from publication and merging.

docs.title: Loaders
docs.text:
One loader per environment; multi-loader means one env per loader. Declare it inside the env block — loader("<name>", "<version>"):

unimined {
    minecraft {
        version = "1.20.1"
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")

        sourceSet("forge") {
            version = "1.20.1"
            loader("forge", "47.2.0")
        }
    }
}

Loader names resolve through the loader registry:

  • Forge is era-aware — loader("forge", …) emits FG1-era wiring on ≤1.7.10, FML-style on 1.8–1.12, and modern Forge ≥1.13 (era examples).
  • Pseudo-loaders — jarmod injects into the MC jar itself (see --jarmod/--jars split|merged); accessTransformer/ accessWidener are transform-only.
  • Products nest loaders — bta { loader("bta-babric", …) }.
  • Single-arg form — inside a named env, loader("0.16.0") reads the lone arg as the version and the env id as the loader name (sourceSet("fabric") { loader("0.16.0") }).
  • Bukkit-family dev plugins — craftbukkit, spigot, and paper stage the dev jar into run/<env>-<run>/plugins/ by default (modDiscovery("plugins")), so the server's own plugin loader discovers it exactly as production does — including plugin.yml/paper-plugin.yml validation and the real plugin classloader (required by JavaPlugin's loader check on Paper). modImplementation plugin deps stage alongside and load for free. Opt back into classpath loading with features { modDiscovery("classpath") } — the ClasspathPluginLoader javaagent then scans source-set output dirs for plugin.yml instead (note: CPL cannot read paper-plugin.yml, so classpath mode only suits plugin.yml-era products).

Loader "api" artifacts resolve via loaderApi — see Dependencies.

docs.title: Adding a loader to an existing project
docs.text:
The manual equivalent of unimined-cli new --loader <name>=<ver>:

  1. Declare the env (a sourceSet env so it doesn't fight the existing main env — or on main for a single-loader project):
unimined {
    minecraft {
        sourceSet("quilt") {
            version = "1.20.1"
            loader("quilt", "0.26.0")
        }
    }
}

  1. Mappings — the env's mappings { } chain (quilt: quiltMappings(...)/hashed(); forge: official()/mcp(...)/ searge(); see Mappings). Nested envs inherit the main env's declarations — override per env as needed.

  2. Metadata — the env's mod { } block emits the loader's descriptor (fabric.mod.json, META-INF/mods.toml, mcmod.info, …): id, name, version, depends — see Mod Metadata.

  3. Sources — env code lives in src/<env>/ (created with the source set); shared code stays in main — aux/sibling envs inherit the parent's classpath via combineWith or implicit parent inheritance.

  4. Runs — <env>Client/<env>Server register automatically; aux flows use datagen()/gametest() (see Datagen/Gametests).

Generating fresh instead? unimined-cli new mymod --loader quilt=0.26.0 emits the same shape — --modules for the per-loader subproject layout.

docs.title: Mappings
docs.text:
Each env declares a mappings { } chain — the sequence of mapping namespaces the env's MC jar and mod deps get remapped through.

unimined {
    minecraft {
        mappings {
            yarn(10)              // fabric yarn
            // official()         // mojang official names
            // mcp("stable", "60") // MCP
            // searge()           // srg names
        }
    }
}

Chain order matters — later entries layer onto earlier ones. The full named-mapping catalog lives in the registry; generator-side, --mappings takes the same DSL lines and --var key=val feeds mapping vars (e.g. Ornithe's ornitheGenVersion).

Mod dependencies declared on env mod* configurations are remapped through this chain automatically.

docs.title: Mod Metadata
docs.text:
mod { } inside unimined { } is the mod identity + runtime metadata, emitted into the loader's descriptor (fabric.mod.json, mods.toml, …) at build time:

  • id, name, version, description, authors, license, url, icon
  • depend(modId, versionRange) — metadata deps
  • loader("fabric") { } / fabric { } — loader-specific sections (entrypoints, extra keys)
  • mixins { create("name") { } } — generated *.mixins.json configs

--metadata dsl on the CLI emits this block instead of hardcoding values in the loader descriptor.

docs.title: Merging with hand-written files
docs.text: If a resource already contains the loader's metadata file (e.g. src/fabric/resources/fabric/fabric.mod.json), the generated document is merged into it rather than colliding: objects merge recursively, arrays union and deduplicate, and generated scalar values win. Only the merged copy ships — the source file is excluded from processResources. Non-JSON collisions still fail the build.

docs.title: Discovery
docs.text:
generate<Env>ModMetadata scans the environment's resources and compiled classes at execution time:

  • *.mixins.json files found in resources are referenced from the mixins array automatically (generated and hand-written configs union, deduplicated).
  • Classes implementing the loader's gametest interface are added to the fabric-gametest entrypoint; FabricClientGameTest implementors land under fabric-client-gametest.
  • Mixin classes are scanned for @Mixin targets × implemented interfaces; each pair becomes a transitive-inject-interface classTweaker rule (generated under META-INF/unimined/injected-interfaces.ct, referenced via classTweakers) and a custom.loom:injected_interfaces entry. Rules already present in the project's own CT/AW files are not re-emitted, and duplicates are suppressed.

Interface-injection names are emitted in the dev namespace; the production repack rebases the metadata keys to the published namespace. Dependent projects receive the injections through the dependency-side classTweaker extraction.

Because generation needs compiled classes, it cannot feed the project's own compile classpath — casts against injected interfaces in first-party sources still need a manual rule. Dependents and the runtime packaging are covered automatically.

docs.title: Datagen and gametest envs
docs.text:
datagen() / gametest() inside an environment declare auxiliary source sets (<env>Data, <env>Gametest). They inherit the parent's version/mappings and see its classes on their classpath, but emit no metadata of their own — the parent's descriptor references their classes (entrypoints, generated data). A second same-id metadata file would collide on the classpath, so generate<Env>ModMetadata no-ops for aux envs.

Server gametests run through the loader's JUnit artifact (fabric-loader-junit) wired onto testImplementation by gametest(). Client gametests additionally arm the env's automatic <env>Client run with the loader's client-gametest JVM args (fabric: -Dfabric.client.gametest -Dfabric.client.gametest.modid=<project>), so runFabricGametestClient boots the client into the test thread and exits — no manual run-config tweaks needed.

docs.title: Multiple Source Sets & Projects
docs.text:
2.0 rewrite. The 1.x unimined.minecraft(sourceSets.x) API moved — envs live in minecraft { sourceSet(...) { } }; see Migrating from 1.x.

Two shapes cover the 1.x use cases:

  • flat — several sourceSet envs in one project;
  • multi-module — a common module + one subproject per loader (what unimined-cli new --modules generates).

docs.title: Flat: one env per source set
docs.text:
Each minecraft { sourceSet(...) { } } block is an independent environment — its own product, loader, mappings, runs:

unimined {
    minecraft {
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")            // env "main"

        sourceSet("forge") {
            version = "1.20.1"
            loader("forge", "47.2.0")
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Sharing between envs
docs.text:
Envs are independent by default; three mechanisms share configuration and classpath:

  • Implicit parent — an env declared inside another env's block (sourceSet("datagen") { datagen() } style nesting, and the datagen/gametest aux verbs) inherits the parent's sections automatically. Opt out with inheritParent.set(false).
  • combineWith(...) — pull another env's declarations in explicitly: combineWith("main"), combineWith("common", env) with sections to take only some (mappings, runs, deps, …).
  • Module deps — modImplementation(project(":common"))-style references share code across projects.

Sibling sourceSet envs at minecraft {} top level don't share — combineWith("main") is the way to layer the main env's config in.

docs.title: Multi-module: common + per-loader subprojects
docs.text:
This is what unimined new mymod --modules --loader fabric=… --loader forge=… emits. Settings includes every module:

A loader module applies unimined, declares its env on main, and depends on :common for shared code:

common gets a loader-less env (MC classpath + mappings only); the loader jars land as modImplementation deps in each loader module. Cross-project inheritance uses the <project>:<env> path form — combineWith(":common:main") pulls the common project's main env (classpath included, so shared code resolves); copyFrom reuses sections without composing output.

docs.title: Products
docs.text:
The product is which Minecraft distribution an env runs — orthogonal to the loader. minecraft { } is the native product; others get their own blocks:

unimined {
    bta { loader("bta-babric", "1.7.6") }       // Better Than Adventure
    reindev { loader("foxloader", "…") }        // ReIndev + FoxLoader
    nsss { file("dist.jar") }                   // Not So Seecret Saturday
    custom("myproduct") { file("custom.jar") }  // arbitrary dist
}

Products nest their loader inside the product env — the loader axis stays the same either way.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text:
Unimined's publish host (xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.publish) turns each bound environment's outgoing artifacts into an adhoc component named unimined<Env> (uniminedMain for main). Destination adapters pick those components up; none of them auto-publish components.java.

plugins {
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined")
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.publish")
}

Auxiliary environments (datagen()/gametest()) are test harnesses — they never produce components or publications.

docs.title: uniminedPublish { }
docs.text:
uniminedPublish {
    javaPublication()                 // opt-in ordinary `java` component
    mavenPublications.set(false)      // opt out of all Maven publications
    environment("main") {
        groupId = "com.example"
        artifactId = "examplemod"
        version = "1.0.0"
    }
}

mavenPublications is on by default: the host applies maven-publish and creates one MavenPublication per unimined<Env> component. Set it to false for component-only or ModPublisher-only builds — no publications are created at all (the publishing { } extension still exists for your own use). javaPublication() opts the ordinary components.java into a java publication — it only takes effect while mavenPublications is enabled, and defaults its artifactId to <project>-java since uniminedMain already claims <project>.

docs.title: Maven
docs.text:
One MavenPublication is created per environment component as it binds — uniminedMain → uniminedMain, uniminedFabric → uniminedFabric, etc. Repositories and credentials are plain Gradle publishing {} config:

publishing {
    repositories {
        maven {
            url = uri("https://maven.example/releases")
            credentials(PasswordCredentials::class)
        }
    }
}

Coordinates default per environment: main publishes as <project.name>; every other environment as <project.name>-<env> (the name-fabric/name-forge convention) — set environment("<env>") { artifactId = ... } to override. Publications that would resolve to identical coordinates fail the build.

Each publication carries the environment's dev and production variants plus sources (Gradle module metadata included): the dev jar rides custom unimined-dev-* usage attributes so plain java-api/java-runtime consumers resolve the production variant unambiguously — request a dev usage explicitly to opt in (see PublishAttributes). publishDev/publishProduction/publishDataFiles on environment("<env>") gate each channel; identity-remap environments publish a single artifact. The loader-merge merged artifact is intentionally not part of the Maven path — it belongs to ModPublisher uploads.

docs.title: ModPublisher
docs.text:
xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.publish-modpublisher feeds artifacts and release metadata into com.hypherionmc.modutils:modpublisher's publisher { } as conventions when that plugin is applied (it stays compileOnly — no ModPublisher classes load unless you apply it). There is no adapter DSL — publisher { } is the single surface for what can't be inferred, and anything you set there wins:

publisher {
    apiKeys {
        curseforge(providers.environmentVariable("CURSE_TOKEN").get())
        modrinth(providers.environmentVariable("MODRINTH_TOKEN").get())
    }
    curseID.set("1234")
    modrinthID.set("abc")
    versionType.set("release")
    debug.set(true)   // dry-run: builds the upload plan, uploads nothing
}

Conventions supplied automatically: artifact (the forgix mergedElements jar when adapter-forgix is applied, else the first bound env's production jar — remap<Env>Jar when it remaps, else jar), additionalFiles (remaining per-loader prod jars), loaders (bound envs' loader names), gameVersions (env versions), and version (project.version). The merged artifact suppresses the per-loader jars; aux envs are excluded; dev artifacts are never uploadable.

docs.title: Manual verification (live upload)
docs.text:
Automated coverage (ProjectBuilder dry-run tests) asserts the config lands on publisher { } — it does not upload. Verifying a real release still needs a human pass:

  • [ ] publishMod with debug.set(true) and a real merged jar — inspect the dry-run plan (files, version, loaders, gameVersions).
  • [ ] Real upload to a staging/draft Modrinth or CurseForge project with scoped tokens via env vars — confirm version, changelog, loaders, game versions, and additional files on the platform UI.
  • [ ] Confirm API keys come from providers only (never literals in the build file) and never appear in logs.

docs.title: Loader-jar merging (forgix)
docs.text:
The adapter-forgix adapter (plugin id xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-forgix) merges per-loader production jars with Forgix's engine:

plugins {
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-forgix") version "..."
}

Every bound environment's production jar feeds mergeLoaderJars automatically (remap<Env>Jar, or jar for non-remapping envs; auxiliary environments are excluded), keyed by loader name — most multi-loader builds need no configuration. Forgix's own plugin isn't required (its DSL only supports multi-project layouts); when applied, its forgix { } merge configurations feed in too, and loaderMerge.from(...) adds or overrides any input. The merged jar is published on the consumable mergedElements configuration (classifier merged) — the ModPublisher adapter prefers it as the upload artifact and suppresses the per-loader jars when it exists. See adapters/forgix.

docs.title: Remap Pipeline
docs.text:
unimined { remap { } } configures the remapping steps — the verbs are ordered pipeline steps applied to the MC jar and remapped mod deps:

unimined {
    remap {
        unpick("path/to.unpick")
        applyClassTweaker { /* custom bytecode transform */ }
        sourceRemap { /* UML source remapper — the default engine */ }
        jst { /* explicit opt-in: Java Source Transform */ }
    }
}

Source remapping runs through UML's source remapper by default; jst { } remains as an explicit engine opt-in for verification or alternate-engine use.

docs.title: Mod artifacts
docs.text:
After the namespace remap step, JAR-surface pipelines automatically run a modArtifacts step that rewrites mod-jar metadata the base remap leaves untouched:

  • kotlin.Metadata internal names (any Kotlin mod jar)
  • mixin configs and refmap emission for jars carrying *.mixins.json
  • JarModAgent/ClassTransform refmaps for jars whose manifest declares JarModAgent-Refmaps

The step is engine-agnostic — it applies identically when remap is overridden with remap("tiny"), and to remapped dependency views, so mod deps get mixin refmaps for the dev runtime. Declare it explicitly with jar { modArtifacts() } only to pin an engine or ordering; it is skipped on identity remaps and on jars without the relevant resources.

docs.title: Standalone artifact remapping
docs.text:
unimined:remap works outside a Minecraft environment — any jar can be remapped between namespaces with remap.artifact(...), which registers a remap<Name>Artifact task:

uniminedRemap {
    artifact("baritone") {
        input.set(layout.projectDirectory.file("baritone.jar"))
        mappings.set(layout.projectDirectory.file("mapping.txt"))
        from.set("target")   // optional — see autodetection below
        to.set("source")
        // output defaults to build/remapped/baritone-remapped.jar
    }
}
// ./gradlew remapBaritoneArtifact

The mapping file is autodetected from its contents at execution time — no format flag is needed:

Format Notes SerializedMappingData bundle Native unimined zip; richest payload (multiple views) MappingBundle JSON Legacy unimined row bundle tiny v1 / v2 Fabric-era standard UMF Unimined Mapping Library universal format SRG / CSRG / package SRG Forge-era formats TSRG v1 / v2 Forge-era formats ProGuard / RetroGuard Common for shipped obfuscated jars (e.g. Baritone) MCP / mcpconfig MCP exports — v1/v3/v6 method+field CSVs, mcpconfig zips Parchment Javadoc/param overlay — must be named parchment.json to autodetect

ProGuard maps are the common case for third-party obfuscated jars (e.g. remapping a shipped mod to readable names). Sidecar formats (AW/AT/CT, nest, exception, signature, unpick) also parse via UML but carry no class-name columns, so they are not useful as a standalone mappings input.

When from/to are unset, namespaces are autodetected from the input jar: the namespace column whose class names best match the jar's contents becomes from, and the single remaining column becomes to. Autodetection fails with an actionable error when no column matches or more than one target candidate remains — set both explicitly in that case.

The step pipeline is shared with the environment machinery — remap { jar { } } declarations apply to artifact tasks too (engine selection via remap("tiny"), access steps, custom steps). Environment-scoped steps and modArtifacts are not applied; those only make sense on environment jars.

docs.title: Production-jar validation (footgunChecks)
docs.text:
After the pipeline, remap<JarTask> (and remap<Name>Artifact) stamps the manifest with Unimined-Mapping-Namespace: <target> — a remapped jar is self-describing — then lints the emitted artifact for packaging mistakes that compile fine but fail at runtime:

  • metadata files parse (fabric.mod.json, quilt.mod.json, mcmod.info, META-INF/mods.toml, META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml, plugin.yml/bungee.yml/paper-plugin.yml, *.mixins.json) and carry their required keys
  • every path the metadata references exists inside the jar: accessWidener files, declared mixin configs, jars[] nested jars, icon files
  • classes named by metadata exist: fabric entrypoints, mixin classes listed in *.mixins.json, the plugin.yml main class
  • the manifest namespace marker is present and matches the target namespace

Findings default to ERROR — the task fails. The level is a remap-block property:

unimined {
    remap {
        footgunChecks.set(FootgunCheckLevel.WARN) // log and continue; OFF disables
    }
}

Sources jars get the marker but skip metadata/class checks (a sources jar legitimately lacks .class files). Only unimined-produced artifacts are linted — third-party jars in transforms are never validated.

docs.title: Run Configs
docs.text: runs { } is top-level. Every environment gets auto-registered run configurations, each materializing a run<Name> task plus IDE run configurations from genIdeRuns.

docs.title: Auto-registered runs
docs.text:
Environment Runs main client, server, prodClient, prodServer <env> <env>Client, <env>Server, <env>ProdClient, <env>ProdServer datagen envs the env's own name (e.g. data → runData) gametest envs <env>Client/<env>Server plus test-task wiring

The prod* variants launch the production-namespace Minecraft artifact with your remapped mod jar — the shipped-runtime check (1.x runObfClient/runObfServer parity).

docs.title: Reaching runs
docs.text:
unimined {
    runs {
        named("client") {           // creates if absent
            jvmArgs.add("-Xmx4G")
        }
        create("ciClient") {        // a custom variant
            prod.set(false)
        }
        runs.configureEach {        // every run
            environmentVariables.put("MC_DEBUG", "1")
        }
    }
}

Tasks are run<Name> — gradle runClient, runProdServer, runFabricData, …

docs.title: RunConfig fields
docs.text: Field Purpose environment which env's classpath/dirs the run launches (convention: the env it was registered for) side CLIENT/SERVER — defaults from the run name prod true = production-namespace MC artifact + remapped jar mainClass launch main class (loader-provided by default) jvmArgs / programArgs launch arguments javaagents file collection rendered as -javaagent: flags (unimined agents attach here — jarmod, expectplatform, CPL) environmentVariables process env stdin piped into the launched process features version-json rule features (is_demo_user, has_custom_resolution) width/height --width/--height args downloadAssets fetch assets before launching (default true) username offline-name shorthand bridging into auth.username auth { } typed session spec — see Auth

docs.title: Argument substitution
docs.text: Loader capability templates and your own args support ${...} launch-property substitution (game_directory, auth_*, classpath, …) plus {modid} — resolved against mod { id } at run time (e.g. fabric gametest's -Dfabric.client.gametest.modid={modid}).

docs.title: Dry-run
docs.text:
-Punimined.run.dryRun prints the assembled launch (main class, args, classpath) instead of exec'ing — the quickest way to inspect what a run would do:

./gradlew runClient -Punimined.run.dryRun

docs.title: IDE integration
docs.text: genIdeRuns emits per-env IntelliJ .idea run XML and Eclipse .launch files for every declared run — regenerate after editing runs { }.

docs.title: Auth
docs.text: See Auth — auth { microsoft() } per run or runs { auth { } } as the default; :loginMicrosoft populates the credential store; unimined.auth.* properties control storage.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.source wires genSources / gen<Env>Sources per bound environment. The default pipeline for an environment with no provider-supplied sources:

  1. Decompile — the env's dev-namespace Minecraft artifact through the selected engine (vineflower by default). The task is @CacheableTask — outputs are content-addressed by input jar, classpath, and engine options, so reruns and shared caches skip work.
  2. Sources-surface steps — the env's RemapSurface.SOURCES pipeline (e.g. uml:remap renaming the decompiled .java to the dev namespace) runs over the decompiled jar when steps are declared.
  3. Linemapped classifier — gen<Env>Linemapped applies the vineflower 0x4646 linemap extras to the binary jar's LineNumberTables, producing -linemapped.jar whose stack traces and debugger line mappings track the decompiled/enriched source lines.

bsm=1 (bytecode source mapping — the linemap extras) is on by default; engine options can override it:

unimined {
    source {
        engine.set("vineflower")
        options.put("bsm", "1")
    }
}

Artifacts land in the env's generated local-repo as minecraft-<env>-<version>-sources.jar and -linemapped.jar.

docs.title: Provider-supplied sources
docs.text: When the product provider ships a devSources artifact (e.g. Forge userdev's mcpconfig chain), the decompile step is skipped entirely — the supplied sources remap straight to the dev namespace.

docs.title: Mod sources
docs.text: genModSources / gen<Env>ModSources remaps the mod's own sources jar through the same SOURCES surface so published -sources classifiers carry the production namespace.

docs.title: Transform hooks
docs.text: unimined { transform { } } wires environment transforms — jar merge, access transforms/wideners, patch application — the surface the transform-* modules plug into.

docs.title: Migrate
docs.text: unimined { migrate { } } and migrateMappings(env) { } handle updating a project across MC/mappings versions — re-emitting sources, moving mappings forward, and fixing up entrypoints for API changes.

docs.title: DSL Index
docs.text:
The 2.0 DSL surface, by extension:

Block Where Purpose unimined { } root top-level plugin extension minecraft { } unimined env bound to a source set (native product) bta/reindev/nsss/custom(n) unimined product envs loader(n, v) env apply a modloader mappings { } env remap chain mod { } unimined mod metadata (id/depends/loader()/mixins) runs { } root run configurations remap { } unimined remap pipeline steps transform { } unimined transform hooks migrate { } unimined migration helpers loaderApi(n, v) unimined loader api coordinates loaderApiModule(n, m, v) unimined one api sub-module modImplementation & co dependencies remapped mod deps (env-scoped)

Member-level detail lives in the API docs (Dokka).

docs.title: Loader descriptor capabilities
docs.text:
Loader descriptors advertise static capabilities through a key→value map; wiring consumes them when envs use the corresponding features. Power users can read them as the descriptor contract:

Capability Consumed by Value shape datagenMain env.datagen() → the run<Data> config main class datagenArgs env.datagen() → program args space-separated args; {output}/{modid} substituted datagenClientArg datagen(client = true) appended flag (e.g. --client) gametestJunit env.gametest() → testImplementation dependency coord; {loader} = loader version gametestClientJvmArgs env.gametest() → <env>GametestClient run space-separated -D flags; {modid} substituted sidedArtifacts loader dep resolution per-side artifact expansion (pre-2.9 foxloader, era splits) jvmTarget/javaVersion run + compile wiring (mc, loader) -> Int? — the runtime bytecode floor modsDir PrepareRunTask staging run mods/ dir capability — dev jars stage in mainClass/tweakClass run wiring loader launch entrypoint replaceLwjgl/replaceLwjglMatch native-era envs LWJGL replacement coord + match rule libraryOverlayMeta Ornithe envs version-manifest endpoint for lib overlays atTool forge envs access-transformer tool coord supportedProducts env binding "*"/exact/"scope:" product whitelist

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
The KDoc/Javadoc API reference is generated with Dokka when the docs are deployed.

Open the API reference

Older per-release API docs are also hosted at unimined.wagyourtail.xyz.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text:
unimined new <name> / unimined init — generate a modding environment for any MC version.

new <name>  — generate a project in ./<name>
init        — generate in the current directory
Flag Meaning --group base package group --version/--mc MC/product version --plugin-version unimined version to apply --loader <name=v> repeat = multiloader; v empty = registry default --product <p> bta, reindev, nsss, custom:<name> --modules common + per-loader subproject layout --dist <path> product jar for custom dists --mappings "<dsl>" mappings chain lines --var k=v mappings-scope variables --side <side> client, server, merged --jarmod JarModAgent transforms (modloadermp shape) --jars split|merged MC jar shape for jarmod-era envs --modid/--package/--name/--mod-version mod identity --metadata dsl emit mod { } metadata block --extra "<line>" raw build.gradle.kts lines --no-wrapper skip gradle-wrapper download --include-build <path> composite pluginManagement resolution --toolchain <n> pin the java toolchain --dsl kotlin|groovy emitted DSL flavor --templates <zip> / --template <name> extract a bundled project zip --out <dir> output directory --gradle include gradlew wrapper files

docs.title: Generation modes
docs.text:
Exactly one layout per project — the CLI picks it from the flag combination:

Mode Trigger Emitted structure FLAT default One module; all envs in a single unimined { minecraft { } } block MULTILOADER --modules common subproject + one subproject per --loader, env per subproject CUSTOM_PRODUCT --product <p> One module; a non-native product env — bta { }/reindev { }/nsss { }/custom("<name>") { } per --product template extraction --templates <zip> (+ optional --template <name>) testing/<name>/ extracted wholesale from a unimined-templates zip — scaffold flags ignored

Era modifiers compose with the layout modes:

Modifier Effect --jarmod client/server source sets, clientJar/serverJar tasks stamping JarModAgent-Transforms, <modid>-<side>.transform stubs --jars split per-side MC jar tasks (jarmod-era; merged = one jar) --side client|server single-side env instead of merged
